method.baseline: Initial working-tree worker executables saved before startup preloading changes; not a clean HEAD build.
method.measurement: Three before/after process pairs per case. First request immediately after ready, then a second request. No primer, cancelled generation, or tokenizer check before requests. A one-second gap allows exited worker resources to be released.
method.request: Hello., en-ja, max_tokens=2; 21 prompt tokens, one output token and one decode to stop. Direct worker pipe timing excludes HTTP/network overhead.
method.precision: Original BF16 weights and FP32 computation in both variants; exact emitted token IDs/text match across cases.
method.startup: Ready waits for bounded matrix preloading and incremental GPU page preparation. No model inference is executed at startup; fused_mlps is zero at ready.
method.memory_caveat: Available memory varies between processes. 8B budgets/retained ranges differ, so its timings include those differences and are not an isolated kernel comparison.
method.concurrency: No other build/test/benchmark from this task ran during recorded startup measurements.

0.8b-metal.limits: Startup cost is reported separately; preloading moves I/O before readiness. No primer, cancelled request or tokenizer subprocess precedes the first request. A one-second gap separates worker processes to allow resource cleanup. System memory pressure and file caches can differ between runs.

limits: Startup work moves before readiness and startup duration increases. It does not guarantee a lower launch-to-answer time.
Unused embedding rows and small CPU weights keep their mapped path; large-projection I/O statistics do not measure all OS page faults.
8B still streams unretained ranges. Readiness is not an mlock guarantee and memory pressure after startup can discard cached ranges.
31B measured only with model-free profiles/builds, not real inference.
